title: Economic sectors sorting cards
subject: Geography
unit: Spring 1: Earning a living and globalisation
source: Seeded from geography/y9 lesson 9 (Economic sectors sorting cards (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 9: What kind of work do we do in the UK? Economic sectors (3.1). To understand how jobs are classified into economic sectors

blocks.title: Sort into: Primary / Secondary / Tertiary / Quaternary
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Quaternary.
blocks.answer: Primary: fisherman; coal miner. Secondary: car assembly worker; builder. Tertiary: teacher; nurse. Quaternary: software researcher; data scientist

questions.q: Classify: a farmer, a baker in a factory, a delivery driver.
questions.model: Farmer: takes from nature: primary. Factory baker: makes things: secondary. Driver: a service: tertiary.

questions.q: Roughly what share of UK jobs are in services?
questions.a: About four in five or more (about 84%)

questions.q: Core: Make a four-column table with five jobs in each sector, including jobs in your own family or community.
questions.a: Correct jobs in each sector, for example primary: farmer; secondary: builder; tertiary: imam, teacher; quaternary: researcher
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: 'Tertiary: imam (a service to the community), teacher, nurse.'

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, describe the UK's employment structure using the pie chart.
questions.a: Description with figures: services dominant about 84%, secondary about 15%, primary about 1%

questions.q: Stretch: Why might a poorer country have far more primary jobs?
questions.a: More people farm and mine; less industry and fewer services

questions.q: Big question: is a farmer, a factory worker or a software designer more important to the economy?
questions.a: All are needed and linked; the UK has most jobs in services, but primary and secondary jobs supply the goods
